overall: The AG found no OML violation: three Board members attending a ZBA meeting, with one speaking as a citizen, did not deliberate, and the AG declined a broad audit of executive session minutes.

allegations.summary: Three Board members attended a ZBA meeting in the same building, and one spoke during public comment, allegedly to influence a ZBA matter; the complaint says this violated the OML.
allegations.key_passage: The quorum of a public body may attend the meeting of another public body “so long as the visiting members communicate only by open participation in the meeting on those matters under discussion by the host body and do not deliberate.”

allegations.summary: Alleged that the three Board members met or deliberated at the ZBA meeting, relying on a photograph of them near the doorway.
allegations.key_passage: As there is no evidence that members of the Board deliberated outside of a meeting, we find no violation.

allegations.summary: In the request for review, alleged the Board improperly reviewed the OML complaint in executive session under Purpose 1.
allegations.key_passage: It is well established that public  bodies may meet in executive session under Purpose 1 to review Open Meeting Law complaints against the body.

allegations.summary: In the request for review, asked the AG to review the Board's executive session minutes from the prior 12 months for compliance with the OML.
allegations.key_passage: Complainants must allege violations with a degree of specificity, as our office will not conduct broad audits of public bodies based on generalized allegations.
